purpose: make capacity follow demand automatically within limits, so users keep their performance and cost stays bounded
entry_criteria: Load profile and performance objectives are known
Metrics for utilization and latency are available
Minimum and maximum capacity limits are agreed with the owner
procedure: Choose scaling signals that track user demand (requests, queue depth, latency) rather than only CPU.
Set minimum, maximum and scaling step values from load-test results, and record why each was chosen.
Set cooldowns and scale-in protection so capacity does not oscillate or drop sessions.
Load test with a rising and a spiking pattern; record time to add capacity and user-facing impact.
Alert on hitting the maximum, on scaling failures and on cost against budget.
Review scaling events monthly and adjust limits.
acceptance_criteria: Latency objective holds during the tested ramp and spike
Minimum and maximum limits are justified
Alerts exist for max reached and scaling failure
Cost is within the agreed bound
validation_method: Service owner and performance engineer review of load-test results.

validation.expect: latency and error thresholds pass; instance count rises as expected

validation.command: kubectl get hpa app -o wide   # example
validation.expect: current replicas between configured minimum and maximum

failure_modes.mode: Scaling is too slow for a spike
failure_modes.detection: Latency exceeds objective during the spike
failure_modes.response: Raise minimum, scale on an earlier signal or pre-warm

failure_modes.detection: Replica count repeatedly goes up and down
Capacity stays at maximum with no demand
failure_modes.response: Investigate the signal and cap with an alert

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A service scales on queue depth with a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 20 replicas. A spike test adds capacity within two minutes and keeps p95 latency under the objective.
